object_types.name: RiskTier

ambiguities.description: Both 'spend tier' and 'risk tier' are colloquially called 'tier' by different stakeholders, causing confusion in conversation even though the system stores them as separate fields. Should the model enforce distinct terminology (SpendTier vs RiskTier) in all user-facing artifacts to prevent ambiguity, and is there any residual case where the terms might still be conflated in reporting or documents?

source_references.excerpt: And you both call it "tier." ... We've asked people to say spend tier and risk tier. Nobody does. It's been a losing battle for two years.

ambiguities.description: Whether the vendor's three addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) should be modeled as separate attributes/entities was mentioned but never resolved in detail -- the transcript only says these are 'frequently different and frequently wrong.' Should each address type be modeled as a distinct value type or fact type, and what identifies/structures an address (street, city, etc.)?

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: The post-suspension handling of in-flight purchase orders (e.g., a possible 'run-off' status) is explicitly unresolved and deferred to a steering group/Legal. The model currently only captures three VendorStatus values and does not capture any rule about PO fulfillment after suspension. This should be revisited once policy is decided.

source_references.excerpt: Then we need a middle state. Something like run-off -- existing POs complete, no new ones can be raised. ... This goes to the sourcing steering group.

ambiguities.description: The transcript states a vendor cannot be moved to active without a completed, signed-off risk review, but does not clarify whether a vendor can transition back from active to draft, or whether suspension requires losing the current review link. The exact set of allowed VendorStatus transitions and their preconditions (e.g., does suspension clear the 'current review' designation?) is not fully specified.

source_references.excerpt: But the system does enforce it -- you cannot move a vendor to active without a completed review, the transition is blocked.
If we suspend a vendor -- their review lapses, or there's a breach, or they turn up on a sanctions list -- what happens to the purchase orders already in flight?

ambiguities.description: Duplicate vendor records (same tax ID, same company onboarded twice) are acknowledged as an ongoing data quality problem but explicitly out of scope. This affects whether TaxId could ever be used for matching/deduplication logic, and whether a future 'parent entity' or 'group' concept is needed to link duplicate/related vendor records for aggregate exposure reporting (as Raj mentions).

source_references.excerpt: We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them. ... Noted, but out of scope for today.
The duplicates are also a compliance problem, for what it's worth. If we've got the same entity twice we can't see aggregate exposure.

ambiguities.description: Mei's informal spreadsheet tracks a 'preferred vendor' flag (used when multiple vendors can supply the same thing) but this was explicitly declared ad hoc and out of the model per stakeholder agreement. It is flagged here only to confirm this exclusion is intentional and not an oversight, and to note there is no formal 'product/category supplied by vendor' concept in the current model even though 'preferred' implies vendors are compared for the same supply category.

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called "preferred." It means if two vendors can supply the same thing, buy from this one. ... It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: The 'Contact' entity's reference_mode (contact_id) is not explicitly discussed in the transcript -- only name, email, and phone are mentioned as attributes. It's unclear whether the system has a formal contact identifier or whether contact is uniquely identified by the vendor+region+some attribute combination (e.g., email). This should be confirmed with Mei/Dana.

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact. Name, email, phone number.
A given vendor in a given region has exactly one primary contact.

ambiguities.description: Whether the 'current' designation of a RiskReview is a stored flag or derived from review date/signed-off status and recency is unclear -- the transcript describes it conceptually ('at most one is the current one') without specifying how currency is determined or stored (e.g., an effective/expiry date field).

source_references.excerpt: A vendor can have several reviews over its life -- we re-review on a cycle, and every re-review is a new record, we don't edit the old one. But one of them is the current signed-off one.
